software.name: Make_Stationary
software.title: Make_Stationary: deseasonalization benchmark for renewable-energy time series (MATLAB)

article.citation: M. Agoundedemba, C. Voyant, M. Despotović, L. A. Garcia-Gutierrez, G. Notton. Does stationarization help? A frugal benchmark of deseasonalization for renewable energy forecasting
article.status: manuscript submitted; no result of it is reported here beyond the repository README

supported: test whether a deseasonalization method helps the final forecast

inputs.definition: nine Corsican series 2021–2023 (GHI, PV, load, wind power, wind speed, temperature, at 30 min or 1 h), included in Data/

outputs.definition: residuals and stationarity diagnostics (PACF, entropy, Lyapunov exponent)
nRMSE, nMAE, nMBE, R², NICE by method and horizon (1 to 6 h)

rules: Never invent a value. Each input is given by the user, an exact unit conversion of a given value, or a documented default that the user explicitly accepts.
Use the canonical unit of each field; convert exactly and say so (for example 2 km -> 2000 m). Never mix a percentage and a fraction.
Ask when a request is ambiguous or a required input is missing; do not infer a number from a place name or a qualitative word.
Run the code unmodified. Report only what was actually computed, with quantity, unit and the input values used; never present a planned or unavailable run as a result.
State the scope and the limits below when you report a result.
Deseasonalization is a selective preprocessing option, to be kept only when it improves the final forecast.
limits: One region, three years, horizons up to 6 hours; the README lists three differences with the manuscript.
